info.title: Dinghy API
info.description: The widget API (`/v1/widget/{key}`, with the visitor's bearer token) and the operator API (`/v1/operator`, with the session cookie, or a workspace API key on the routes whose security lists `apiKey`). MCP lives at `/v1/mcp`, with an API key. Every error answer is `{ error: { code, message } }`, and clients branch on `code`. Sign-in lives at `/v1/auth`, a BetterAuth pass-through that is not part of the versioned API.

visitorToken.description: The browser token from POST /v1/widget/{key}/visitors, or a host token: an HS256 JWT that the host site signs with the workspace's signing secret.

sessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
sessionCookie.description: The session cookie that POST /v1/auth/magic-link/verify sets when it uses a sign-in link (BetterAuth). The cookie is `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` on https. A write must also send the server's own Origin.

apiKey.description: A workspace API key, `dk_...`, that an owner or admin creates in Settings. It works only in its own workspace, with a member's permissions: read, search, reply, close, reopen, snooze and assign conversations. It needs no Origin.

setupKey.description: A workspace API key, `dk_...`, made with Full access, the `setup` level. It reaches what a Chats (`conversations`) key does, and the webhooks: list, add, change, delete, rotate a secret, test and read deliveries. It never reaches keys, members, billing, export or the workspace's deletion.

get.summary: Stream the visitor's messages after a cursor
get.description:
Server-sent events: `message` (its id is the new cursor, its data a Message, which an edit or a delete sends again: replace it by its `id`), `ready` when caught up, `resync` to load from the start, `notice` for something live that is not stored, and `close` with a reason. A `notice` has no id and may be lost: `{ kind: "typing", name, typing }` while an API key's bot writes a reply, and with `typing: false` when it stops. Read this with fetch, because EventSource cannot send the bearer token.

A `close` event's data is `{ reason }`: `lifetime` (the stream reached its 15-minute cap), `expired` (the host token expired), `revoked` (access was taken away, such as a block, a suspension or a removal), `unauthorized` (the token or session is no longer valid), `stopping` (the server is shutting down) or `error`. Reconnect from the last cursor, except after `unauthorized`, which needs a new token or sign-in.

post.summary: Report the page the visitor is on, for operators
post.description: The widget sends this when it loads and when the page's address changes, and only for a visitor who already has a token because they used the chat. The server stores something only for a visitor who has a conversation, and never creates a visitor here. It keeps the origin and path, never the query or hash, the title, when it came, and a short device line made from the User-Agent, which it does not keep. Each report adds a row to the visitor's page journey, unless it repeats the newest one, and a visitor keeps the newest 100.

post.description: The loader sends this when the page loads and once a minute while the tab is visible, with or without a token. It sets no cookie and stores no ID in the browser: the tab's ID lives in the page's memory. The server looks up the country of the request's address and drops the address, and keeps the tab only in Valkey, for 90 seconds after its last beat. For a visitor with a token, it saves the country and time zone on the visitor.

post.description: `locale` is the widget's language, which the visitor's reply emails, transcripts and chat page use. `context` holds unsigned values from the host page, such as a plan or a cart total, that operators read next to the visitor. They are not verified. Each report replaces the last one: at most 20 keys of 1 to 40 characters, with a string of up to 200 characters, a number, true, false or null as each value. The widget sends a report on each page load for a visitor who has used the chat, and again after the first message. The server keeps it only for a visitor who has a conversation, and never creates a visitor here.

get.summary: Stream the workspace's changes after a cursor
get.description:
Server-sent events: `change` (its id is the new cursor), `ready` when caught up, `resync` to load everything again, `notice` for something live that is not stored, and `close` with a reason. With no cursor, the stream starts at the present, so load the lists after `ready`.

A `change` event's data is `{ kind, conversationId }`, with `conversationId` null for a workspace change. A `message.created` change also has `fromVisitor`, true when the visitor wrote it. The kinds are `message.created`, `message.updated` (an operator edited a reply), `message.deleted`, `conversation.closed`, `conversation.reopened`, `conversation.assigned`, `conversation.snoozed` (snoozed or unsnoozed), `conversation.deleted`, `conversation.moderated`, `conversation.handled` (a person or a bot took it), `conversation.labeled` (a label was put on or taken off), `draft.changed`, `transcript.requested`, `team.changed`, `billing.changed` and `workspace.changed`. A client reloads what the kind names, and ignores a kind it does not know.

A `notice` has no id and may be lost. Its data is `{ kind: "typing", conversationId, visitorId, draft }`, a visitor's unsent text, empty when they stopped, `{ kind: "bot_typing", conversationId, name, typing }` when an API key types or stops, or `{ kind: "receipts", visitorId }` when a visitor read replies or a reply email went out, so load the conversation's messages again.

A `close` event's data is `{ reason }`: `lifetime` (the stream reached its 15-minute cap), `expired` (the host token expired), `revoked` (access was taken away, such as a block, a suspension or a removal), `unauthorized` (the token or session is no longer valid), `stopping` (the server is shutting down) or `error`. Reconnect from the last cursor, except after `unauthorized`, which needs a new token or sign-in.

post.summary: MCP (Model Context Protocol) over Streamable HTTP, stateless, with JSON answers
post.description: One JSON-RPC 2.0 message per request. Protocol 2026-07-28 is stateless: each request names its version in `params._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]`, its `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers must match the body (400, -32020 otherwise), and its methods are `server/discover`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`. The versions 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26 use `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`. An unknown version answers 400 with -32022 and the supported list. Every key gets `list_conversations`, `search_conversations`, `get_conversation`, `reply`, `close_conversation`, `reopen_conversation`, `snooze_conversation`, `unsnooze_conversation`, `assign_conversation`, `add_note`, `list_drafts`, `hand_off`, `list_members`, `list_saved_replies`, `set_typing`, `wait_for_messages`, `get_contact`, `list_contacts`, `search_contacts`, `get_live_visitors` and `get_analytics`, in the key's workspace. A Setup key also gets the webhook, install, allowed site, appearance and test visitor tools. A notification gets 202 with no body. A tool that fails answers with `isError: true` and the error's stable code. `GET` answers 405, because there is no event stream.

get.summary: Stream the workspace's events to an API key's bot, with no public server
get.description:
Server-sent events with the same `type` and `data` as webhook bodies, in the key's workspace. Each event's name is its type, and its data is `{ type, workspaceId, data }`. Its id is its position: reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` or `?after=` to resume after it. When one change makes several events, such as `conversation.created` then `message.created`, each has its own position, `generation.seq.part`, and the last has the change's cursor, `generation.seq`. With no cursor it starts now. `resync` means the cursor is too old: read the open conversations again. `ready` comes when caught up. Heartbeats come every 25 seconds, the stream ends after 15 minutes, and it takes a slot in the workspace's stream limit. A revoked key's stream ends within 25 seconds.

A `notice` has no id and may be lost: `{ kind: "typing", conversationId, draft }`, a visitor's unsent text, only while the workspace shows typing previews. Messages from test visitors come with `conversation.visitor.isTest: true`.

A `close` event's data is `{ reason }`: `lifetime` (the stream reached its 15-minute cap), `expired` (the host token expired), `revoked` (access was taken away, such as a block, a suspension or a removal), `unauthorized` (the token or session is no longer valid), `stopping` (the server is shutting down) or `error`. Reconnect from the last cursor, except after `unauthorized`, which needs a new token or sign-in.
